cite: Overseers of the Poor v. Somerset County Poor District, 168 Pa. 286
holding_summary: The court held that although the pauper James McFadden had previously acquired a settlement in Somerset County, he later gained a new settlement in Spring Township by being hired and serving there as a servant for a full year, notwithstanding that during the same period he boarded and lodged with his mother, a boarding-house keeper, in the neighboring borough of Bellefonte.

quotes.text: that she kept a boarding house in said borough, that the said James boarded and lodged with her, paying his board as a stranger
Held, that he gained a settlement in Spring township.

notes: Boarding-house/paid-lodging arrangement (mother as keeper, son as paying boarder) is incidental background fact for a poor-law settlement dispute; the court never adjudicates the legality or character of the letting itself, so treatment as 'favorable' reflects only that the arrangement is described without any suggestion of impropriety.

cite: Fessenden's Estate (B. A. Tyler's Appeal), 170 Pa. 631
holding_summary: The court held that a testamentary charge for a beneficiary's support is not extinguished under the 21-year limitation acts so long as the devisee who accepted the charge continued to perform it, and that upon successive sales of the charged land the tracts must be exhausted in the inverse order of their alienation.

quotes.text: the said F. A. Fessenden, assisted by his said wife, Eliza, kept a boarding house in the borough of Montrose, Pa., the profits of which were the principal source of support of the said Fessenden family

We agree with the learned court below in its conclusion that the charge upon the Tyler lot is not extinguished by the act of April 27, 1855, P. L. 369, or by the supplement thereto of Feb. 2,1869, P. L. 3.

notes: Boarding house is incidental background establishing the devisee's livelihood; the case's actual holding concerns extinguishment of a support charge on land, not the legal character of the boarding arrangement. Duration of individual boarders' stays is not stated.
